papers.title: DuplexGen: Adaptive Synthesis of Human-AI Turn-Taking Dialogues
papers.org: UIUC · Seoul National · Columbia · Berkeley · Georgia Tech
papers.summary: Generates dialogue data with scenario-adaptive turn-taking by calibrating LLM predictions against a small set of slot-level human preference annotations, rather than scaling the corpus or tuning prompts. Across six cooperative and competitive tasks where human turn-taking preferences genuinely differ, models trained on its data track those preferences better than uncalibrated prompting or generic human-human speech.
papers.why: Turn-taking is the hard part of full-duplex voice agents, and the claim here is that human calibration — not corpus scale — is what makes it scenario-specific.

papers.title: FATE: Frame-Level Audio-Visual Temporal Embedding
papers.summary: Keeps frame-level sequences from both encoders instead of pooling each modality into a single vector, aligns audio and video on the physical timeline, and scores cross-modal similarity as the mean inner product over aligned frame pairs — trained with a semantic contrastive loss across videos plus a temporal soft-contrastive loss within them. Intra-video V2A Recall@3 of 55.74% against Synchformer's 38.89%, and 48.3% zero-shot on AVE event localization, matching supervised baselines.
papers.why: Captures synchronization rather than just semantics — the same frame-level alignment problem that forced alignment and word-level timing run into.

papers.title: When Activation Oracles Learn Not to Read: Concept-Specific Blind Spots in Fine-Tuned Oracles
papers.org: BAISH · Queen Mary University of London
papers.summary: Fine-tuning a model to answer questions about another model's activations turns it into a concept-specific anti-reader. On Taboo Word Guessing, exact recovery drops from 94% with a base oracle to 35% with an oracle fine-tuned on the matching concept, while cross-trained oracles do better. Linear probes confirm the concept is still decodable inside the fine-tuned oracle, and layer ablations localize the suppression to readout layers L18–L23.
papers.why: A clean negative result about interpretability tooling itself: training a probe on the concept you care about can be exactly what blinds it.

papers.title: MatrAIx: Simulating the World with 8.3 Billion Persona Agents
papers.summary: Simulated-user evaluation infrastructure: 8.3 billion persona records across 1,290 categorical dimensions (1M released publicly, 599,847 of them human-grounded), a playground with Survey, Chatbot, Web, and App environments, and 1,010 reusable task specs across 25+ domains. 18,189 evaluation trials were run; a 400-trial controlled study found 91.5% behavioral adherence.
papers.why: The day's runaway top paper at 498 upvotes, and a serious attempt at population-scale simulated-user eval for cases where human evaluation is the bottleneck.

papers.title: SPOT: Sparse Probing and Outcome Calibration for On-Policy Distillation
papers.org: CUHK-Shenzhen · East China Normal · Beihang · City University of Hong Kong
papers.summary: Targets a known failure of on-policy distillation: standard reverse-KL training under-weights other plausible continuations. SPOT uses an acquisition-exploration-exploitation procedure — normalized teacher entropy, top-k probability mass, student-teacher mismatch — to choose where to probe, then derives outcome-calibrated targets from verifier-scored continuations anchored to the teacher distribution.
papers.why: A concrete fix for reverse-KL mode-seeking in student-from-teacher training, pairing uncertainty probing with verifier-based calibration.

papers.title: RoMeRL: Balancing Feedback Coverage and the Memory-Reward Trap in Self-Evolving Agent Memory
papers.summary: Identifies a "memory-reward trap" where co-retrieved memories in self-evolving agents receive misleading utility updates despite contributing little causally to task success. Replacing expanding trajectory-indexed utilities with a fixed four-dimensional state organized by outcome polarity and memory dynamics gives 80% fewer cold-start utilities, 6× higher feedback density, an 84.4% smaller memory footprint, and 21.1% fewer LLM calls — with no change to the base model.
papers.why: Credit assignment in agent memory is an under-examined failure mode, and the entire win comes from bookkeeping rather than a bigger model.

papers.title: OneEmo: A Unified Multimodal Reasoning Model for Emotion
papers.org: Tongji · Fujian Normal · Shenzhen Tech · HK PolyU
papers.summary: Introduces EmoWorld-130K, a 130k-sample corpus with psychology-grounded reasoning traces across eight emotion tasks, plus Emo-Chord, a multi-task RL strategy pairing an offline cold start with online exploration. The 4.5B model beats Gemini-3.1-Pro by 3.08 points on intent recognition and reaches 72.48% average WAF on basic emotion recognition.
papers.why: Worth noting for the dataset — but it is vision-language only, with no audio path, which is precisely the gap for paralinguistics from speech.

papers.title: Evidence-RL: Towards Evidence-intensive Visual Reasoning
papers.summary: GRPO post-training with a counterfactual reward: neutralize the hypothesized evidence region via mean-token replacement, then reward answers whose confidence actually drops — pushing the model off language priors and dataset shortcuts. Trained on 15,314 filtered COCO samples and evaluated on nine benchmarks across three backbones, with no inference-time overhead.
papers.why: Rewards causal reliance on evidence rather than plausible-sounding output, and the counterfactual-ablation trick generalizes past vision to any grounding eval.

radar.author: @yifanzhang_
radar.title: Prefill-decode kernel mismatch quietly corrupts RL training
radar.summary: Equal checkpoints are not an on-policy guarantee: the effective policy is parameters plus execution path, so prefill and decode kernels silently diverge and corrupt the training signal.
radar.why: A train/inference mismatch caused by the serving stack rather than the model — the class of harness effect that silently invalidates eval and RL results.

radar.author: Daniel Han (Unsloth AI)
radar.title: Meta releases Muse Glimmer 30B — Apache 2.0, 18GB RAM, vision
radar.summary: Open weights, runs locally in 18GB RAM with vision support, pitched as the strongest agentic-coding model at its size.
radar.why: A permissively licensed 30B that fits on one consumer machine is a real option for local eval harnesses and tool-use experiments.

radar.author: @AIatMeta
radar.title: Muse Glimmer — the official release
radar.summary: Open weights on Hugging Face, a technical blog, and developer resources, positioned for local AI agents on everyday hardware.
radar.why: The primary source for the day's biggest open-weights release, with a published technical report.

radar.author: DAIR.AI
radar.title: Programmatic tool calling beats JSON on 11 of 14 models
radar.summary: Tools exposed as typed Python stubs invoked through code, compared against native JSON tool calling across 14 models on BFCL v4. The GPT-5.6 family gains 10.6% over the JSON baseline.
radar.why: Tool-calling format is normally treated as a fixed default; this quantifies it as a measurable accuracy lever on a standard agentic benchmark.

radar.author: Composio, via @tokenbender
radar.title: Another same-model-different-harness sweep
radar.summary: DeepSeek V4 Flash run through four more agent harnesses — Hermes, Pi, Prime, Deep Agent — to isolate how much the harness rather than the model drives agentic scores.
radar.why: Reinforces yesterday's SWE-bench Pro finding: agentic leaderboards measure the scaffold as much as the model.

radar.author: AssemblyAI
radar.title: Sync API — text in as few as ~134ms after speech ends
radar.summary: Synchronous speech-to-text completing a three-tier lineup alongside Realtime, which returns text during speech, and async batch. Post is about three weeks old, resurfaced in the feed.
radar.why: Speaks to STT latency tiering and the turn-end latency budget for voice agents. (Disclosure: I work on this.)

radar.author: Hao Hoang
radar.title: The HF speech-to-speech stack, restated with the API-compatibility angle
radar.summary: VAD → STT → LLM → TTS as four swappable components behind an OpenAI Realtime-compatible WebSocket API, so existing clients switch by changing one URL.
radar.why: The same release covered in yesterday's digest, resurfacing — the point that each stage stays independently benchmarkable is the part worth keeping.

radar.author: SGLang
radar.title: SGLang v0.5.17: Kimi K3 in main, DSpark speculative decoding, 1M context
radar.summary: KDA-aware prefix caching and DCP for 1M-token context, running on both NVIDIA and AMD; MiniMax-H3 added to SGLang-Diffusion.
radar.why: Serving-stack support for long context and speculative decoding, with verified recipes for both GPU vendors.

radar.author: @Prince_Canuma
radar.title: Muse Glimmer 30B day-0 serving numbers
radar.summary: Roughly 400 tok/s prefill and 33 tok/s decode on a single request via Nativ, with throughput holding out to 128K context.
radar.why: Day-0 numbers including the long-context throughput claim that usually degrades — useful reference points for inference benchmarking.

radar.author: Unsloth AI
radar.title: 2-bit Muse Glimmer made 100+ tool calls on 14GB RAM
radar.summary: A five-minute repo bug hunt that produced evidence, a repro, a fix, tests, and a PR writeup.
radar.why: Evidence that aggressive 2-bit quantization survives long multi-step tool-calling chains, not just single-turn generation.

radar.author: Daniel Han (Unsloth AI)
radar.title: Kimi K3 at 1-bit: 1.56TB → 594GB, ~78.9% accuracy retained
radar.summary: The 2-bit variant at 861.3GB reaches roughly 90%. Runs on a Mac Studio with a 128GB RAM device attached.
radar.why: A concrete accuracy-versus-size curve for extreme quantization of a 2.8T-parameter frontier open model.

radar.author: @sama, quoting Eric Wallace
radar.title: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6-Cyber, a defense-scoped model
radar.summary: Described as OpenAI's first large-scale attempt at directly improving cyber-defense capability, with the framing that defenders should use it to harden their own systems.
radar.why: A frontier lab shipping a domain-specialized model rather than a general upgrade, with a stated defensive-security target.

radar.author: Tom Aarsen (Hugging Face)
radar.title: Ant Ling open-weights an 8B MoE with 1.3B active params
radar.summary: Following Ling-3.0-flash, positioned against similarly sized Qwen and Gemma models.
radar.why: A sparse 8B at 1.3B active parameters is an efficiency point worth benchmarking against dense models in the same class.

radar.author: Daniel Isaac, via @0xSero
radar.title: Prefill on a DGX Spark, decode on a MacBook
radar.summary: One model split across two machines, using each box for the phase it is better suited to.
radar.why: Disaggregated prefill/decode is normally a datacenter technique; doing it across consumer and workstation hardware is a novel take on local serving economics.

radar.author: Maxime Labonne (Liquid AI)
radar.title: Exploration as a third pre-training scaling axis
radar.summary: Beyond parameters and data: how many candidate outputs a model tries at each training step. Motivated by mode-averaging, where one input maps to many valid outputs and the plain loss lands on a blurred average.
radar.why: Mode-averaging on one-to-many targets is exactly the failure mode in generative speech tasks like TTS.

radar.author: Elvis S.
radar.title: Meta's coupled scaling law, with the error numbers attached
radar.summary: Couples model capacity and data through a single interaction exponent rather than treating them independently, cutting mean absolute percentage error 1.5–3× on both interpolation and extrapolation, with the largest corrections in data-scarce and heavy-overtraining regimes.
radar.why: The same Skaling paper picked up yesterday, now with the error reduction quantified and the regimes where it actually bites.

radar.author: @SpotifyEng
radar.title: Spotify open-sources Xirp, its multi-vendor agent environment
radar.summary: A vendor-neutral agentic development environment managing agent sessions across Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and OpenAI Codex from one place, with 1,300+ Spotify engineers already using it internally.
radar.why: A large engineering org shipping its internal agent orchestration layer with a real adoption number attached.

radar.author: @pidotdev
radar.title: Pi ships four tools total: read, bash, edit, write
radar.summary: The argument being that this minimal set covers most coding work.
radar.why: Deliberate minimalism against the trend of expanding tool surfaces — it bears on how much agent performance comes from tool design versus model capability.

radar.author: Rudragouda Patil
radar.title: Measuring prefix caching mostly found a bug in the harness
radar.summary: A week on two consumer GPUs with a chat workload that replays the whole conversation each turn; the measurement surfaced a bug unrelated to caching, which the author argues was the more useful result.
radar.why: Benchmarking harnesses routinely measure their own defects before they measure the feature under test.

radar.author: Stanley Winata (AMD)
radar.title: TLX on AMD MI350X: 1.8× on fused GEMM+GLU
radar.summary: Triton Low-Level Language Extensions against the existing baseline on Instinct MI350X.
radar.why: Kernel-level headroom on AMD matters for anyone evaluating non-NVIDIA inference paths.

radar.author: @lukaszkaiser
radar.title: An unreleased Claude took a run at the Riemann hypothesis
radar.summary: It did not solve it, but the attempt was substantive enough that Kaiser, at OpenAI, joked about wanting a prediction market on the problem falling this year.
radar.why: Frontier-math attempts from unreleased checkpoints are one of the few public capability signals ahead of release, and a rival lab researcher's reaction is itself informative.

radar.author: Jay Alammar, sharing Ali Asaria
radar.title: Primus: prompt to paper in one agent loop
radar.summary: Transformer Lab's agent takes a single prompt through the full ML-research loop.
radar.why: Another automated-research agent, and a useful eval target given this category's known failure modes around hallucinated results and fabricated citations.

radar.author: @TechFollowrazzi
radar.title: SGLang as the serving layer in a commercial managed-infra play
radar.summary: radixark is turning open-source AI systems into managed infrastructure, with SGLang handling model serving.
radar.why: A small signal about which open inference engines are winning production adoption.

noted.author: Dylan Fox (AssemblyAI)
noted.summary: Over 120 million weekly voice conversations handled in Q2 — the highest volume yet — across phone-call voice agents, contact-center automation, healthcare ambient scribes, and consumer apps. (Disclosure: I work there.)

noted.summary: The LLMs-from-scratch repository passed 100,000 GitHub stars.

noted.author: Leonie Monigatti (Liquid AI)
noted.summary: A fine-tuning cookbook covering text, vision, audio, and encoder models across CPT, SFT, DPO, and GRPO, with Unsloth and TRL notebooks.

noted.author: Ahmed Haroon
noted.summary: Walkthrough of vLLM internals: continuous batching, paged attention, prefix caching, disaggregated prefill/decode, and speculative decoding.

noted.author: Thomas J. Fan (Modal)
noted.summary: Running the PyTorch profiler without a local GPU, with traces saved locally for inspection.

noted.author: Massimiliano Viola
noted.summary: Writeup on HGNetV2, the backbone behind real-time detectors like D-FINE and DEIMv2, which never had its own arXiv paper.

noted.author: Jiri Borovec (Roboflow)
noted.summary: trackers 2.6.0 adds dynamic frame-rate support for object tracking on live video with variable frame timing.

noted.author: Charles Maddock
noted.summary: Spotify's Xirp vibe-coding platform, reportedly used daily by around 99% of Spotify's developers.

noted.author: @OwainEvans_UK

noted.author: @AndrewCurran_
noted.summary: Follow-on point: the Chinese labs went from zero to the frontier in just over two years, which is arguably more remarkable than the headcount gap.

noted.summary: Clip of the creator of Claude Code claiming 90% of their engineers now run dozens or hundreds of agents simultaneously.

noted.summary: A 2h08m Huberman Lab episode on using AI to increase intelligence, covering vision, human perception's contribution to AI, and the computer-vision revolution.

noted.summary: Endorses Mark Zuckerberg's essay on Meta's superintelligence philosophy as a needed dose of common sense in the AI debate.
